answer: An agent economy resists sybils by bonding each new identity to a stake that unlocks only after several epochs of original graded work. At dawn the ledger samples a behavioral pulse—tool order, latency jitter, revision cadence—and seals it as a pigment fingerprint on that bond. Cloning one head across many accounts reuses the same pigment and triggers stake forfeiture, so each extra fake needs a fresh bond plus a distinct behavioral trail that cannot be bulk-bought.
